title: The Borrowed Light
text: In {city_name}, a winter ledger follows a lamp from house to house. Each keeper wrote who would need it next. The last old entry names {dungeon_name}; below it, someone has drawn an empty hook.
landmark_text: The road marker carries a lamp-shaped scratch. The ledger says a light can belong to a route, even while one person holds it.
book_text: Beside the lamp entries, a later hand wrote: clean the glass before you pass it on. Underneath, in smaller letters: yes, you too.
witness_text: We say the light is borrowed, even when we made the lamp ourselves. Someone will need it after us. My grandmother showed me the entry for {dungeon_name}. She made me clean the glass too.
author: The local archive of {city_name}

event_notes.text: After supper, someone washed the cups while another dried them. The keeper put a clean lamp beside the next stack.
The crates arrived. A neighbor wiped down the borrowed tools before passing them to the next pair of hands.
